summary: LLM inference costs are dominated by token usage, and most production systems leave significant savings on the table by sending redundant context, re-running identical queries, and routing everything to premium models. Combining caching, compression, and model routing commonly cuts API spend by 40-80% while improving latency (time-to-first-token improvements of 13-31% from prompt caching alone). These optimizations are stackable and mostly low-risk, making them among the highest-ROI engineering work available.

techniques.name: Prompt (Prefix) Caching
techniques.description: Reuses the cached KV state for a repeated prompt prefix (e.g. a shared system prompt or long document) so the model skips recomputing those tokens during the prefill stage. It reduces input-token cost and improves time-to-first-token, but the model still performs normal decoding to generate the response.
techniques.savings: 41-80% cost reduction on cached input, 13-31% faster time-to-first-token
techniques.example: Place your large, static system instructions and reference documents at the start of the prompt and mark them as cacheable (Anthropic cache_control or OpenAI automatic prefix caching) so repeated requests only pay full price for the variable user portion.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Matches incoming queries by meaning using embedding similarity rather than exact text, and can return a cached response without invoking the model at all. It saves both input and output tokens, unlike prefix caching which saves only input, and works best under user-defined error-rate or similarity thresholds.
techniques.savings: 30% token spend reduction at ~45% cache hit rate; up to 50%+ in high-repetition workloads
techniques.example: Embed each incoming query, search cached embeddings for cosine similarity > 0.85, and if a match is found return the stored response ('How do I return a product?' matches 'What's your return policy?') instead of calling the LLM.

techniques.name: Exact-Match Response Caching
techniques.description: Caches the full response to identical queries at sub-millisecond latency, avoiding the LLM inference call entirely for repeated requests. It is the simplest cache layer and pairs well with semantic caching in a multi-tier strategy.
techniques.savings: 20-50% cost reduction in workloads with high query repetition
techniques.example: Hash the normalized request (model + messages + params) and store the response in Redis with a TTL, serving cache hits directly for FAQ-style or dashboard-refresh traffic.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduces the number of input tokens by sending only relevant summaries instead of full context, trimming boilerplate, and compressing retrieved documents. Advanced systems summarize long context while preserving output quality.
techniques.example: Run retrieved RAG chunks through a compressor like LLMLingua or a cheap summarization model before injecting them into the prompt, sending a condensed version instead of raw full documents.

techniques.name: Model Routing
techniques.description: Routes each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, sending simple queries to small/fast models and reserving premium models for complex tasks. This is one of the highest-ROI optimizations because most traffic does not need a frontier model.
techniques.savings: 20-50% cost reduction (routing ~70% of traffic to cheaper models is common)
techniques.example: Use a lightweight classifier to send straightforward queries to GPT-4o-mini or GPT-3.5-class models and escalate only ambiguous or multi-step reasoning tasks to a premium model like GPT-4o or Claude Opus.

techniques.name: Output Token Control (Max Tokens & Formatting)
techniques.description: Caps and shapes the generated response, since output tokens are typically billed higher than input tokens. Requesting concise or structured output and setting a sensible max_tokens prevents runaway generations.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens to a realistic limit and instruct the model to 'respond in at most 3 bullet points' or return JSON only, avoiding verbose explanations you will discard.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Groups multiple independent requests into a single batch or uses provider async batch APIs that offer discounted pricing for non-latency-sensitive workloads.
techniques.savings: Up to 50% via provider batch-API discounts
techniques.example: Submit overnight bulk classification or enrichment jobs through OpenAI's Batch API to get a 50% discount versus synchronous calls.

techniques.name: KV Cache Management (Infrastructure)
techniques.description: On self-hosted inference servers, techniques like cache eviction (dropping low-importance tokens), cache compression (quantization/pooling), hybrid memory offloading to CPU/NVMe, and novel attention mechanisms reduce memory pressure and serving cost. A March 2026 Dell survey found no single technique wins — combination strategies perform best.
techniques.savings: Varies; combination strategies yield the largest throughput/cost gains
techniques.example: Deploy vLLM with PagedAttention and enable KV-cache quantization plus CPU offload to serve more concurrent requests per GPU without increasing hardware.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLM queries that stores responses and returns cached results for semantically similar prompts using embeddings and a vector store.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); self-hosted infrastructure costs only

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: In-memory data store supporting exact-match and vector-based semantic caching for LLM responses, enabling multi-tier caching with sub-millisecond exact-match lookups.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis Cloud paid tiers from ~$5/mo; Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, model routing, fallbacks, rate limiting, and cost tracking across providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, cost analytics, caching, and prompt management via a drop-in proxy.

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in LLM caching (in-memory, SQLite, Redis, semantic), prompt management, and routing abstractions.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression toolkit that compresses prompts (up to ~20x) while preserving task performance, reducing input tokens for long-context and RAG prompts.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API gateway that routes requests across many providers/models with automatic fallback and price-based routing to the cheapest suitable model.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-token passthrough with small routing fee

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference server with PagedAttention, KV-cache optimization, prefix caching, and quantization for cost-efficient self-hosted serving.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); GPU infrastructure costs only

quick_wins: Enable provider prompt/prefix caching by putting large static system prompts and reference docs at the start of your requests — near-zero effort for 40-80% savings on cached input and faster responses.
Add an exact-match response cache (e.g. Redis keyed on the normalized request) to eliminate duplicate inference calls for repeated queries.
Set a realistic max_tokens and instruct models to be concise or return structured output to cut costly output tokens.
Route traffic with a cheap classifier so simple queries hit small models (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) and only hard tasks reach premium models, cutting 20-50% of cost.
Drop in a gateway like LiteLLM or Helicone to get caching, routing, and per-model cost visibility so you can measure hit rate and spend before optimizing further.
